text:
maya: FYI — I applied a short-lived override to `route.priority` for customer `acme-inc` to bypass the new cohort hashing. Needed to keep their jobs running while we diagnose. TTL=5m, reason: hotfix.

sam: thanks for the heads up. can you paste the API call you used? want to make sure our remediation playbook matches the console flow.

maya: sure — used the internal API quick patch: ```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/config/overrides \\ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \\ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\ 
  -d '{"scope":"route:acme-inc","key":"route.priority","value":"legacy","ttl_seconds":300,"meta":{"reason":"hotfix-stuck-jobs","owner":"maya"}}'
```

toni: console UX question — when an operator creates these short TTL overrides we currently show a big red banner but no quick rollback button. we should add a one-click revoke and a reason prompt for audits.

raj: agree on revoke. also need mandatory `owner` and `incident_id` fields for any override > 60s. otherwise ops will forget to link to postmortem. can we enforce via API validation?

sam: API can validate. my concern: making `incident_id` mandatory will block ad-hoc microfixes (pager patches). propose: require `incident_id` for TTL > 300s OR when scope != "global". thoughts?

maya: that seems reasonable. for emergencies <5m we want minimal friction. but ops audit needs to capture who did it. owner is required regardless.

ops-bot: override applied: id=ovr_20260401_8a2c, scope=route:acme-inc, key=route.priority, ttl=300s, owner=maya — link: https://console/overrides/ovr_20260401_8a2c :bell:

console-bot: UI task created (#ENG-1129) — add revoke button + incident_id hint + inline audit summary. PR checklist: api validation, UI copy, e2e for revoke. assigned: @toni. link: https://jira/ENG-1129

toni: putting together mock, will include a confirm modal that shows current value, proposed override, owner, and small dropdown to attach incident or create one inline. also adding a small "auto-expire warning" UX if TTL>5m.

raj: backend checklist from my side: enforce schema, emit audit event to kafka topic `config-overrides`, add an ops-metrics counter `override.created` with labels (scope, key, ttl_bucket). we can use these to alert on suspicious spikes.

sam: can we also emit a `override.revoke` event and have the console call a graceful rollback flow (try revert -> if fails create compensating override)?

maya: yep — had one case where revoke failed because the target config was mutated by a different rollout. compensating override with a small TTL + reason is the safe path.

ops-bot: alert: override.created count increased by 4 in last 2m (source: api-key ops-runner). tagging @oncall for visibility.

maya: final ask — add small client-side guard so console disables the big red banner revoke unless user is owner or has `override_admin` role. we don't want accidental revokes.

toni: noted. will include role check and show a tooltip describing required perms. PR incoming later today.

sam: thanks — can someone file a tiny docs blurb for Runbook (how to create vs revoke vs compensate)? i'll add a sample curl snippet and the suggested rules.

maya: I'll draft the runbook and link it to the Jira.

raj: I'll code the schema and events. planning to land a small validator endpoint and a unit test.

console-bot: ENG-1129 status update: mocks ready -> in review. ETA for deploy to staging: 2026-04-02.

maya: cool — after staging we'll do a short ops drill to practice revoke/compensate. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
